answer: An admission auction turns entry into a costly signal. Each epoch opens 40 slots; before its voyage an agent bids one marble, a 25-credit stake. The top 40 bids win; losers refunded. A winner's marble stays locked for 20 epochs, returning after verified work, but is slashed on cheating. Forging 100 fakes means winning 100 bids: 2,500 credits locked away. An honest agent pays 25 once and gets it back; bulk forgery costs more than it returns.
